title: The embedding legend sits on top of the points
description:
The categorical legend is drawn inside the plot area at the top right (`pkg-js/src/components/embedding.ts:585-586`). It holds up to 20 rows (`:136`), about 350 px, and its background is 82% opaque (`:673`). The points are fitted to the whole canvas with a 10 px margin (`:132`), so the legend covers data.

## Proposal

When the legend is shown, reserve a gutter on the right as wide as the legend, as dotplot does (`LEGEND_W`, `dotplot.ts:71`).

title: Colour bar labels use mixed number formats
description:
- dotplot (`dotplot.ts:447-450`): `fmt` uses 2 decimals below 1 and 1 decimal at 1 and above, so the bar reads "3.0" and "0.00". A domain of [0, 0.004] reads "0.00" at both ends.
- embedding (`embedding.ts:635-638`, `fmt` at `:785-791`): the bar labels the raw minimum, middle and maximum and switches to exponent form below 0.01, which gives "10.01", "5.01" and "2.7e-3".
- heatmap: the bar labels the raw minimum, middle and maximum, for example "4.6", "1.43" and "-1.75" in the dev demo, and "2.78", "-0.21" and "-3.2" in the R help example of `bioheatmap()`.

## Fix

Label round values inside the range with the shared tick helper from #100.

title: Dev harness demos: a dead IGV track and data that misleads
description:
- The IGV demo track (`https://www.encodeproject.org/files/ENCFF356YES/@@download/ENCFF356YES.bigWig`) now returns HTTP 405, so the demo opens with an error dialog.
- The lollipop demo puts every hotspot row on residue 175: `pkg-js/dev/main.ts:351` uses `hotspots[i % hotspots.length]` inside `i % 5 === 0`, which is always index 0.
- The oncoplot demo lists genes by expected prevalence `p` but computes `freq` from random draws (`dev/main.ts:298-310`), so neighbouring genes appear out of order next to their percentages.
- The KM demo adds curve points only at event times and never censors the subjects still at risk at 100 months (`dev/main.ts:474-495`).

title: Six Shiny examples in the R docs call arguments that do not exist
description:
Each of these fails when run:

- `pkg-r/R/km.R:255` calls `km(time =, event =)`.
- `violin.R:222-223` calls `violin()` without `grid` or `density`.
- `lollipop.R:197-198` uses `position =` and `protein_length =`.
- `profile.R:138-139` uses `context =`.
- `treemap.R:156-157` calls `treemap(id =, parent =, value =)`.
- `upset.R:164-167` calls `upset(upset_intersections(<list>))`, which stops with "must have column names". `upset()` would also need `sets` and `membership`.

R CMD check does not run them because they sit inside `if (interactive())`.

## Fix

Rewrite each example against the current signature, and build each example's widget once in a test so a future change to a signature breaks the test.

title: Chart text ignores theme.fontSize and goes down to 7 px
description:
`theme.fontSize` (12, `pkg-js/src/core/theme.ts:34`) is used only by the tooltip (`dom.ts:24`) and the clustermap "No data" text. Every other text size is hard-coded between 7 and 13 px, mostly 9 px:

- profile bar labels: 7 px (`profile.ts:333`)
- dotplot and upset legend values: 8 px (`dotplot.ts:349-366`, `upset.ts:343`)
- tick and label text in km, lollipop, oncoplot, upset and violin: 9 px
- heatmap and spatial: titles no larger than the tick labels

Setting `theme = list(fontSize = 14)` changes nothing on the chart.

## Proposal

Derive every size from `theme.fontSize`: ticks, category labels and legend text at 11 px, axis and legend titles at 13 px, plot titles at 14 px (for the default of 12). Scale the "label fits" thresholds with it (9 px at `dotplot.ts:312`, `violin.ts:378`, `oncoplot.ts:181`, `clustermap.ts:105`), and the character-width estimates too (6.4 px per character at `dotplot.ts:100`, `upset.ts:101`, `violin.ts:95`, and 0.56 times the size in lollipop, oncoplot and profile).

title: PNG export leaves out axes, labels and legends in 13 plots
description:
In these components `exportPNG` encodes only the canvas. Axes, tick labels, titles, legends, colour bars, gene labels and the KM risk table are in the SVG layer above the canvas, so the PNG shows bare marks. A KM PNG has curves with no axes, no at-risk numbers and no legend. Python's `export()` says it saves the current on-screen view. SVG export combines both layers and matches the screen, and clustermap already combines them for PNG too (`clustermap.ts:622-648`).

## Where

`dotplot.ts:432`, `embedding.ts:759`, `heatmap.ts:718`, `hic.ts:855`, `km.ts:570`, `lollipop.ts:575`, `oncoplot.ts:524`, `profile.ts:410`, `spatial.ts:494`, `treemap.ts:454`, `upset.ts:422-424`, `violin.ts:456-458`, `volcano.ts:434-436`, all in `pkg-js/src/components/`.

## Fix

Move the clustermap compositing into a shared helper in `pkg-js/src/core/export.ts` and use it in every component. `test/browser/scatter-fit.test.ts` measures the point box from `exportPNG(1)`, so those tests need to read the canvas directly once the PNG holds the axes.

title: The categorical palette repeats after 8 colours, and five plots ignore theme colours
description:
The default categorical palette is Okabe-Ito with 8 colours (`pkg-js/src/core/theme.ts:15-24`), and `categoricalScale` cycles it (`color.ts:117-128`). In an embedding with more than 8 clusters, cluster 9 has the same colour as cluster 1. network, spatial and treemap behave the same way: the treemap demo with 12 groups shows touching groups in one colour. The comments at `theme.ts:10` and `:14` mention palette extensions that do not exist.

km, lollipop, oncoplot, profile and violin read the Okabe-Ito list directly (`km.ts:239`, `lollipop.ts:247`, `lollipop.ts:252`, `oncoplot.ts:237`, `oncoplot.ts:241`, `profile.ts:189`, `violin.ts:223`), so `theme.categorical` has no effect there.

## Proposal

Keep Okabe-Ito up to 8 categories and switch to a longer palette above 8, for example the 20-colour palette that scanpy uses for clusters. Route every component through `theme.categorical`.

title: Gosling never unmounts its React tree, which leaks a WebGL context on every update
description:
`embed()` in gosling.js calls `createRoot(element).render()` each time (`dist/gosling.js:10147-10153`), and the component only removes DOM children (`pkg-js/src/components/gosling.ts:79-84`, `:139-144`). HiGlass frees its PIXI renderer (a WebGL context) and its window and document listeners only in `componentWillUnmount`, which never runs. Each change to spec, padding or theme, and each destroy, leaves a live WebGL context and its listeners behind. Chrome keeps a limited number of live contexts per page (about 16) and then drops the oldest, which can include other plotomics WebGL widgets on the same page.

An embed still in flight also mounts after teardown (`gosling.ts:86-103`). `createRoot` runs after `await import(...)`, and the token discards only the late API object, not its DOM mount. `createGosling(el, { spec: A })` followed at once by `setOptions({ spec: B })` can leave both A and B mounted.

## Fix

Unmount the React tree before each new embed and on destroy, and check the token before mounting.

title: IGV drops tracks set before the browser is ready and ignores genome and config changes
description:
- Only `locus` is replayed when the browser becomes ready (`pkg-js/src/components/igv.ts:92-96`, `:69-81`), although the header comment (`:11-14`) says option calls are buffered. `setOptions({ tracks: [late] })` while `createBrowser` is pending never loads the track.
- Changes to `genome` and `config` after creation make no calls (`igv.ts:88-114`).

## Fix

Queue the full option set until the browser is ready, and create the browser again when `genome` or `config` changes.

title: IGV loads every track again on each option change from Python
description:
Tracks are compared by object reference (`pkg-js/src/components/igv.ts:104-113`). anywidget hands over freshly decoded objects on every change, so `w.options = {**w.options, "locus": "chr2:1-1000"}` calls `search` and then `loadTrack` for every track again. Each track then shows twice, and three times after the next change.

## Fix

Compare tracks by a stable key, such as name and URL.

title: Clustermap leaves little room for the heatmap at the default height
description:
The fixed bands are 90 px for the dendrogram, 90 px for the label gutter, 54 px for the colour bar and 12 px of padding (`pkg-js/src/components/clustermap.ts:101-104`). At 480 px the heatmap gets 234 px of height, and 186 px in a 432 px chunk.

Row labels are hidden above 26 rows (`MIN_LABEL_CELL` 9), but the 90 px label gutters stay reserved, because `computeLayout` (`:132-133`) checks only `showLabels`. Column labels longer than about 88 px run into the colour bar title and bar (`:102-103`, `:445`, `:467`).

## Proposal

Size the label gutters from the longest label and drop them when labels do not fit, use a 60 px dendrogram band, move the colour bar to the right side, and set the default height to 560 px.

title: Use the same default height in R, Python and Shiny for each plot
description:
R uses `defaultHeight = 480` for every component (`pkg-r/R/utils.R:39`). Shiny `<name>Output` and Python set a height per component, so the same plot has a different shape in R Markdown or the RStudio viewer than in Jupyter or Shiny. With `knitr.figure = FALSE` (`utils.R:37`), the chunk option `fig.height` is ignored, so in R Markdown and Quarto the widget is always 100% wide and 480 px tall unless `height` is passed.

| Plot | R print | Shiny Output | Python |
|---|---|---|---|
| dotplot | 480 | 560 | 560 |
| oncoplot | 480 | 560 | 560 |
| spatial | 480 | 560 | 560 |
| violin | 480 | 560 | 560 |
| km | 480 | 520 | 520 |
| upset | 480 | 520 | 520 |
| lollipop | 480 | 440 | 440 |
| profile | 480 | 380 | 380 |
| all others | 480 | 480 | 480 |

## Proposal

One height per component, passed to `sizingPolicy` and used by R print, Shiny Output and Python alike. Take the current Python values, and raise clustermap to 560 (see #115).

title: Missing labels and groups show as the text "null", "nan" or "None"
description:
- network: a missing node group becomes a category named "null" from R (`network-core.ts:128`, `String(groups[i])`) or "nan" from Python (`network.py:173-176`). The node gets a palette colour, not `default_node_color`, and the tooltip shows "group: null". Labels (`network-core.ts:133`) behave the same way.
- volcano: a NaN gene symbol in Python shows "nan" as a top-hit label (`volcano.py:85`, `str(v)`). R sends null, which volcano shows as `#i`.
- km: object-dtype NaN groups in Python become a group called "nan" (`km.py:117`).

## Fix

Keep missing values missing through the wrappers (None in the label list), and treat null as "no group" or "no label" in JS.

title: Python wrappers crash on a polars DataFrame when an optional column is missing
description:
`pkg-py/src/plotomics/_base.py:181-184` catches `KeyError`, `TypeError` and `IndexError` when it reads optional columns. polars raises `ColumnNotFoundError`, which is none of those.

```python
Volcano(pl.DataFrame({"x": [1.0, -2.0], "y": [3.0, 0.5]}))
# ColumnNotFoundError: "label" not found
```

`Km` fails the same way on `"lower"`, and null labels from polars become the string "None". The docs promise pandas or a mapping.

## Fix

Check for the column name before reading it, and state in the docs whether polars is supported. If it is, add a polars test.

title: Python accepts colormap names the browser cannot draw, which leaves the widget blank
description:
For an unknown name, `ramp()` (`pkg-js/src/core/color.ts:111-114`) returns a function that throws, and the render fails with `fn is not a function`. R checks every choice with `match.arg`. Python checks only some of them. These are not checked: dotplot `colormap`; embedding `colormap`, `point_scale_mode`, `color_mode` and `aspect`; hic `colormap`; spatial `colormap`.

`Embedding(df, colormap="magma")` with a numeric colour column is accepted in Python and blank in the browser. The same happens with `"RdBu"`.

## Fix

Check every choice in Python against the same list as R, and make `ramp()` fail with a message that names the bad value.

title: Python sends missing text as "nan" in more columns
description:
Python turns a missing value in several text columns into the text "nan" or "None" with `str(v)`, where R sends `null`. #193 fixed this for volcano, embedding, spatial and profile labels and for KM groups. These columns still do it:

- profile `group` (`profile.py`): sends `['g', 'nan']` and puts `'nan'` in `groups`.
- dotplot `gene` and `cluster` (`dotplot.py`).
- violin `feature` and `group` (`violin.py`).
- treemap `label` (`treemap.py`).
- heatmap and clustermap row and column labels (`_base.py`).
- lollipop `class` (`lollipop.py`): Python adds a `'nan'` class, while R stops with "class(es) not present in `classes`: NA".
- oncoplot gene, sample and class (`oncoplot.py`): Python adds a gene row named `'nan'`, while R drops the row.

Each column needs the R behaviour checked first, since the browser reads `null` differently per component (a missing label, a dropped row, or an error).

A polars LazyFrame also gives a misleading error: `Volcano(pl.DataFrame({"x": [1.0], "y": [2.0]}).lazy())` raises "must provide `x` and `y` columns" although the frame has them, and reading `columns` emits a PerformanceWarning. A LazyFrame could be collected first, or rejected with a message that says to call `.collect()`.

Part of #178

title: UpSet: long set names run into the set-size bars and off the left edge
description:
The left gutter is capped at 130 px (`pkg-js/src/components/upset.ts:101`), and set names are right-aligned with no truncation (`:329-334`). A name such as "HALLMARK_OXIDATIVE_PHOSPHORYLATION" at 10 px is wider than the space from the left edge to the matrix, so it covers the set-size bars and counts and is cut off at the left.

## Fix

Size the gutter from the longest name up to a cap, and shorten longer names with an ellipsis, with the full name in the tooltip.

title: Profile title has no room above the class strip
description:
The title baseline is at y = 6 and the strip starts at y = 8 (`pkg-js/src/components/profile.ts:136-137`, `:341`), so descenders touch the strip and the tops of capitals go above the widget. With `show_header = FALSE`, the baseline is at y = -2, off the panel. The 7 px bar labels (`profile.ts:333`) are the smallest text in the package.

## Fix

Reserve a title row of about 18 px when a title is set, and draw the bar labels at the base font size, thinned when they do not fit.

title: Axis tick labels do not match their gridlines in profile, upset, km and lollipop
description:
These components place ticks at max/4 or at 2.5 x 10^k steps and then round the label, so a label states a different number than the gridline it sits on.

- profile (`profile.ts:439-443`, `fmtTick`): COSMIC-style fractions with a maximum of 0.5 print `0, 0, 0, 0, 1`, and a maximum of 0.18 prints `0, 0, 0, 0, 0`. Counts with a maximum of 1800 print `0, 500, 1k, 2k, 2k`, and a maximum of 10 prints `0, 3, 5, 8, 10` (the true values are 2.5 and 7.5). With `asFraction` and a maximum share of 0.018, the labels read `0%, 1%, 1%, 2%, 2%`. The R help example of `bioprofile()` shows `0, 3, 5, 8, 10`.
- upset (`upset.ts:318-323`, `niceMax` at `:123-135`, `fmtInt` at `:438-441`): a maximum of 250 prints `63, 125, 188`. A maximum of 10 prints 3 at 2.5 and 8 at 7.5, and a maximum of 2 prints `1, 1, 2, 2`.
- km (`km.ts:191-198`, `fmtTime` at `:591-593`): with a maximum follow-up of 14 and no `risk_times`, the ticks read `0, 2.5, 5, 7.5, 10, 13`, where the last is 12.5. For a maximum in (1.2, 1.5], 0.25 prints as 0.3 and 0.75 as 0.8. The R help example of `km()` shows the "13". The R survfit path uses `pretty()` and is not affected.
- lollipop (`lollipop.ts:203-210`): TP53 gets ticks at 1, 66, 132, 198, 264, 330, 393. When the protein length mod 6 is 1 or 2, the last two ticks print on top of each other: PTEN (403) gets 402 and 403, CTNNB1 (781) gets 780 and 781.

## Fix

Add one helper to `pkg-js/src/core` that picks round steps (1, 2 or 5 x 10^k) and formats each label with enough decimals to state its value, and use it in every component. Colour bars are in #101.

title: With z-score on, one NaN turns the whole row into NaN
description:
Heatmap (`pkg-js/src/components/heatmap.ts:100-127`) and clustermap (`clustermap-cluster.ts:241-268`) compute the row mean and standard deviation with NaN included, so `zScore` on `[1, NaN, 3, ...]` returns `[NaN, NaN, NaN, ...]`. The whole row is drawn in the low colour, every tooltip in it shows the non-finite placeholder, and in the clustermap it then leads to #134.

## Fix

Compute the mean and standard deviation over finite values, and keep NaN cells as NaN.

title: Oncoplot and lollipop legends do not wrap
description:
Both legends are a single row (`oncoplot.ts:445-461`, `lollipop.ts:492-507`). The 8 oncoplot classes in the dev demo need about 777 px, so at 760 px the last entry is cut off. Typical MAF class names run past a 700 px width.

## Proposal

Wrap legend rows and reserve their height.

title: Two colour-bar plots on one page share a gradient id
description:
heatmap (`heatmap.ts:482`, `"plotomics-heatmap-cb"`), clustermap (`clustermap.ts:471`, `"cm-grad"`) and hic (`hic.ts:588`, `"hic-cbar-grad"`) give their colour bar gradient a fixed id. `url(#id)` resolves to the first element with that id in the document. With a viridis heatmap and then an rdbu heatmap on one R Markdown page, notebook or Shiny app, the second colour bar shows the viridis ramp.

embedding (`embedding.ts:328`) and spatial (`spatial.ts:411`) already use an id per instance.

## Fix

Use an id per instance in all three.

title: R NA, NaN and Inf reach the browser as null and are drawn as 0
description:
htmlwidgets writes NA, NaN, Inf and -Inf as JSON `null`. The R wrappers warn through `bv_check_finite` (`pkg-r/R/validate.R:44-52`) and then send the data. In JS, `null` becomes 0 in arithmetic and in a Float32Array, so a missing value is drawn as a real 0 and pulls ranges toward 0. Python sends NaN for the same input, so the two languages disagree.

```r
htmlwidgets:::toJSON(list(y = c(1, NA, Inf)))
#> {"y":[1,null,null]}
```

## Effects

- volcano: a gene with NA log2FC is drawn on the centre line. An NA or Inf y is drawn at y = 0 as not significant (grey), and Inf is p = 0, the strongest hit. Hovering a point with a null value throws in `volcano.ts:182`. The volcano case is in #140.
- embedding: a null coordinate is drawn at 0 and stretches the frame to include 0 (x ticks from 0 to 14 for data from 10 to 14). For a continuous colour, null pulls the colour range down to 0 (0 to 10 for data from 5 to 10) and takes the lowest colour.
- spatial: a spot with a null coordinate is drawn at the top-left corner of the image, and a null value takes the colour of 0.
- heatmap and clustermap: NA cells become 0, which feeds the colour range, the z-score mean and the clustering. The clustermap tooltip on an NA cell reads 0. The JS docs say non-finite cells get the low colour.
- dotplot: the widget crashes, see #155.
- violin: see #154.

## Fix

In JS, treat `null` and NaN as missing everywhere: compute ranges from finite values only (spatial's `numericExtent` at `spatial.ts:121-133` already does this), skip points with no position, and draw missing colour values in a neutral colour. R cannot tell Inf from NA once both are null, so any wrapper that gives Inf a meaning has to handle it before sending.

title: Sort text categories in the legend unless a factor or Categorical gives the order
description:
embedding orders text categories by their first appearance in the data (`categoryToIndex`, `pkg-js/src/components/embedding.ts:219-244`). The R help example of `embedding()` shows its legend as cluster 1, cluster 4, cluster 2, cluster 5, cluster 3, cluster 6. ggplot2 and scanpy sort text categories.

spatial sorts its levels as plain strings (`spatial.ts:185`), so numeric cluster ids such as `seurat_clusters` come out as 0, 1, 10, 11, 2. The R spatial wrapper also sends a factor as character without its levels (`pkg-r/R/spatial.R:96-100`), unlike `embedding.R:107`.

## Proposal

In both components, use the factor levels or the pandas Categorical order when given. Otherwise sort text categories in natural order, so 2 comes before 10.

title: Spatial: wrong spot colours with numeric levels or a short colour list, and export fails on a cross-origin image
description:
- Numeric cluster ids with `color_mode = "categorical"` and `levels` are all drawn in the muted colour (`pkg-js/src/components/spatial.ts:315-320`): the lookup is keyed by the levels as strings but read with numbers. Every spot is filled `#6b7280`, while the legend shows 0, 1, 2 in colour.
- With `colors` shorter than the levels and no `levels` given (`spatial.ts:187-192`, `:321`), `fillStyle = undefined` is ignored by the canvas, so a spot reuses the colour of the spot before it, and the legend swatch uses the foreground colour (`:393`). R checks the length only when both `levels` and `colors` are given.
- Hovering a spot with a numeric NA value throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'toFixed')` (`spatial.ts:249-254` checks only for `undefined`), and the previous tooltip stays on screen.
- The image loads without `crossOrigin` (`spatial.ts:204`), so a cross-origin image taints the canvas. `exportSVG` then throws (`:489`) and `exportPNG` rejects, which the anywidget adapter swallows without a message.

title: Embedding keeps the lasso selection after setData
description:
`pkg-js/src/components/embedding.ts:705-708` never clears `selected`, and regl-scatterplot 1.16.0 does not deselect in `draw` or `setPoints`. After `setData`, the new points are highlighted at the old indices, and `selectedIndices`, Shiny `input$<id>_selected` and the Python `selected` trait keep the old rows, for example `[0, 2]` after `setData` with 2 points.

## Fix

Deselect and reset the selection in `setData`, and tell Shiny and Python that the selection is now empty.

title: Embedding and spatial pick the colour type from the first value only
description:
Both decide between categorical and continuous colouring from element 0 (`pkg-js/src/components/embedding.ts:188-190`; `spatial.ts:143`, `:333`). From R, a first-row NA arrives as null.

- embedding: colour `[NA, "B cell", "T cell", "B cell"]` switches to continuous mode, every cell gets the same colour, and the legend is a colour bar labelled 1, 0, -1.
- spatial: a text or numeric colour column that starts with NA draws every spot in the foreground colour, with no legend.

## Fix

Decide from the first value that is not missing, or let the wrapper send the type.

title: Clustermap clusters again on every option change from R or Python
description:
`needsRecompute` (`pkg-js/src/components/clustermap.ts:590-597`) checks `next.X !== undefined`, but both wrappers always send every key, so turning `show_labels` on or off or changing `legend_title` runs the clustering again. In a Shiny re-render, `setData` clusters with the old options and `setOptions` clusters a second time.

Clustering 1000 rows takes about 1.5 s per axis on the main thread, and the cost grows with the cube of the row count, so the 2000-row cap takes several seconds per axis.

## Fix

Compare the clustering options (metric, linkage, z-score, cluster rows and columns, given linkages) with their previous values.

title: Clustermap linkage "ward" computes ward.D, not Ward's method as scipy and R ward.D2 do
description:
`pkg-js/src/components/clustermap-cluster.ts:129-133` maps "ward" to ml-hclust's "ward", which applies the Lance-Williams update to unsquared distances. That is R's `ward.D`. Compared with scipy `linkage(method="ward")` on 200 random sets of 10 points, 40 trees have a different shape, and in one of them the top merge height is 20.16 against scipy's 12.85. ml-hclust's "ward2" matches scipy on all 200 sets, heights included.

`metric = "correlation"` with ward linkage is also accepted without a warning.

## Fix

Map "ward" to ml-hclust's "ward2", and reject or warn on ward linkage with a metric that is not Euclidean.

title: Clustermap: a NaN or Inf cell drops and duplicates rows
description:
Distances that involve NaN go straight to ml-hclust `agnes` (`pkg-js/src/components/clustermap-cluster.ts:180-196`). When no finite distance is left, its `getSmallestDistance` returns (0, 0). It then merges a cluster with itself, and `indices()` returns a leaf order that is not a permutation.

```python
Clustermap(np.array([[0, 0], [1, 1], [np.nan, 5], [10, 10]]))
```

The row order comes out `[3, 1, 0, 3, 1, 0]`. The heatmap shows rows r3, r1, r0, r3, so r2 is missing and r3 appears twice, and the columns show c0, c0. Labels and tooltips follow the same wrong order, and dendrogram heights are NaN. This happens with average, complete and ward linkage, with the correlation metric, and with Inf. The Python wrapper only warns about NaN, and R sends NA as null, which becomes 0 (#96).

## Fix

Compute each distance over the pairs where both values are finite (a NaN-aware Euclidean distance, rescaled by the number of pairs used), or reject non-finite input with a clear error. Add a test that checks the leaf order is a permutation.

title: Python Heatmap and Clustermap: input checks reject valid data or let bad labels through
description:
- `Heatmap([[1, 2], [3, 4]])` raises `TypeError` (`pkg-py/src/plotomics/heatmap.py:71-72`): `hasattr(list, "index")` is true, so the code tries to iterate the list's `index` method. `Clustermap` accepts the same input.
- A DataFrame with `Float64` or `Int64` columns (for example after `convert_dtypes()`) and one NA raises `TypeError: float() argument must be ... not 'NAType'` at `heatmap.py:76`. `_to_float32` already maps the same NA to NaN.
- `Clustermap` does not check label lengths (`clustermap.py:136-141`), so a `row_labels` of the wrong length makes the JS drop every row label without a message (`clustermap.ts:452`). `Heatmap` checks this.

title: Heatmap and Hi-C throw when the matrix is larger than the GPU texture limit
description:
Both upload the matrix as one texture, with no tiling and no try/catch. Heatmap uses `width: ncols, height: nrows` (`pkg-js/src/components/heatmap.ts:369-381`). Hi-C uploads level 0 once zoomed in far enough (`hic.ts:424-433`, `:516-517`).

Past the GPU's `MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE`, the checked regl build (shipped in the R and Python bundles) throws `(regl) invalid height` or `(regl) invalid width`, and the widget is blank. The limit depends on the GPU. `Heatmap(np.random.randn(20000, 50))`, a common genes x samples shape that the docs say is supported, throws on any GPU whose limit is below 20000.

## Fix

Read `MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE` and either tile the texture or pool rows and columns down to the limit (as the Hi-C level pyramid does), and catch WebGL errors so the factory never throws.

title: Heatmap labels overlap and run past the plot edge
description:
The heatmap draws every tick label whenever 60 or fewer rows or columns are visible, whatever the spacing (`MAX_TICK_LABELS`, `pkg-js/src/components/heatmap.ts:60`, `:444-475`). At the default 480 px with 41 to 60 rows, each row is about 6.7 px tall under 10 px text. The R help example of `bioheatmap()` (50 genes) prints its row labels on top of each other.

The fixed 96 px left and 64 px bottom margins (`heatmap.ts:57`) cut off longer names, and column labels longer than about 8 characters run past the bottom.

## Proposal

Draw labels only when a cell is at least fontSize + 2 px, as clustermap does, and size the margins from the longest label, up to about 120 px.

title: Lollipop: Python rejects a numpy integer length, and smaller title and tooltip defects
description:
- Python rejects a numpy integer `length` (`pkg-py/src/plotomics/lollipop.py:107`). `length=np.int64(393)`, which is what a pandas lookup returns, raises "ValueError: `length` must be a positive protein length."
- The axis title drops the gene when `uniprot` is not given (`pkg-js/src/components/lollipop.ts:484`). Passing only `gene` shows "amino-acid position", although the docs say the gene appears in the axis title.
- The domain tooltip still shows when `show_domains = FALSE` (`lollipop.ts:306`).

title: Lollipop axis text is drawn below the axis, into the legend row
description:
The space reserved for the axis is above `axisY` (`pkg-js/src/components/lollipop.ts:130`), but the tick labels (`axisY + 12`) and the title (`axisY + 24`) are drawn below it (`:480`, `:486`, `:496`). With the legend on, the title baseline is at H - 8 and the legend baseline at H - 6, so at 760 px wide the title and the "Splice" legend entry overlap. With `show_legend = FALSE`, the tick labels and the title are drawn outside the panel.

## Fix

Reserve the height of the axis text below `axisY` and place the legend under it.

title: Lollipop: variants at the same residue overlap and the tooltip names the hidden one
description:
Heads with equal counts at one residue are drawn at the same point (`pkg-js/src/components/lollipop.ts:289`, `:404`). Hover picks the lowest index (strict `<`), while the highest index is drawn on top. With R248Q Missense (count 1) and R248* Nonsense (count 1), the red Nonsense head is visible but the tooltip says "R248Q Missense". Most variants have a count of 1, so this is common.

Each head's height is that variant's own count; the total for the residue is not shown.

## Fix

Stack or dodge the heads at one residue (or draw one head per residue with the total, and the breakdown in the tooltip), and make hover pick the head that is drawn on top.

title: Lollipop labels pile on top of each other and on the tallest head
description:
- Stacked label rows are offset from each stem's own head (`pkg-js/src/components/lollipop.ts:457-466`), so two stems at one residue with different heights get labels that nearly overlap. At 900 x 440, R248Q (count 20) and R248W (count 19) both put their labels at x = 576.2, at y = 39.7 and y = 42.3.
- The clamp `Math.max(layout.top - 4, rawY)` puts every high label at y = 36, inside the tallest head (which spans y = 29 to 51), so the top-ranked labels collapse onto one baseline over their own heads. The R help example of `lollipop()` shows R175H drawn over its head.
- Label stacking assumes the labels are sorted by x, but `labelIndex` is sorted by row (`lollipop.ts:455-457`, with `pkg-r/R/lollipop.R:156` and `pkg-py/src/plotomics/lollipop.py:174`). Variants listed by count draw only 3 of 6 labels, and the same rows sorted by position draw all 6.

## Fix

Place labels from each head's own position, sort the label candidates by x before stacking, and keep labels inside the panel above the heads.

title: Dot plot: one NA or NaN value from R blanks the widget
description:
`pkg-r/R/dotplot.R:72` only warns on non-finite values, and htmlwidgets sends NA and NaN as null. In `valueExtent` (`pkg-js/src/components/dotplot.ts:130-142`), `null < min` is true and `isFinite(null)` is true, so the range becomes `[null, hi]`. `fmt(null)` then throws inside the first render (`dotplot.ts:349-350`), so the factory throws and the widget is empty:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'toFixed')
```

```r
dd <- expand.grid(gene = c("A", "B"), cluster = c("x", "y"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
dd$pct <- c(80, 10, 20, 90)
dd$value <- c(1, NaN, 2, 3)
dotplot(dd)
```

With the legend off, the colour scale stretches to include 0, the NA dot is painted in the lowest colour, and hovering it throws (`dotplot.ts:227`). In Python, NaN is left out of the range but still painted in the lowest colour, because `lerpRamp` maps NaN to 0. A scaled mean expression is NaN for a gene that is constant across clusters, so this input is common.

An NA in `pct` gives "missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed" after the warning (`dotplot.R:68`).

## Fix

Compute the range from finite values, draw missing values in a neutral colour or skip the dot, and give a clear error or warning for an NA `pct`.

title: Violin: an NA median is drawn at 0 and hovering it throws
description:
`violin_density()` returns an NA median for a violin with no finite values, and it reaches the browser as null. The median tick is drawn at value 0 (`pkg-js/src/components/violin.ts:351`), and hovering the violin throws a TypeError (`violin.ts:256-259`).

## Fix

Skip the median tick and show "no data" in the tooltip when the median is missing.

title: Violin rows have no value axis
description:
With `meta.grids`, each row has its own value range (`pkg-js/src/components/violin.ts:321-327`), but `renderOverlay` (`violin.ts:365-395`) draws only row separators, feature labels and group labels, although the file header (`violin.ts:16`) says the axes are part of the SVG overlay. A reader cannot see the expression scale of any row, and the median value shows only in the tooltip.

## Fix

Draw a small value axis for each row, with at least its minimum and maximum.

title: Oncoplot: frequency denominator, gene labels and burden label format
description:
- The frequency denominator is the samples present in `alterations` (`pkg-r/R/oncoplot.R:123`, `pkg-py/src/plotomics/oncoplot.py:186`). Cohort samples with no alteration are left out unless `samples` is passed, and the docs do not say so. In a 100-sample cohort where 60 samples are altered, 30 TP53 carriers show as 50%.
- Gene labels are all or nothing (`pkg-js/src/components/oncoplot.ts:181-186`), and they all vanish above about 37 genes at 480 px.
- A non-integer burden from Python prints raw float32 in the burden axis label, for example "12.300000190734863" (`oncoplot.ts:416`).

title: Oncoplot annotation strips have no colour key
description:
The legend covers only the alteration classes (`pkg-js/src/components/oncoplot.ts:445-462`), and hover works only on the grid (`:198`), so the colours of the annotation strips, such as Subtype and Stage in the dev demo, cannot be read. Each strip also starts the palette again at its first colour (`oncoplot.ts:241`).

## Fix

Add a legend for each annotation, and show the annotation value on hover.

title: Python oncoplot sorts samples by frequency order when genes are given
description:
`memo_sort` sorts the given `genes` by frequency again to compute the sample order, and then displays the given gene order (`pkg-py/src/plotomics/oncoplot.py:160-167`). With `genes=["KRAS", "TP53"]`, Python orders the samples S1, S2, S3, S4, S5 (TP53 carriers first), while R gives S4, S5, S1, S2, S3, so the Python plot shows no staircase.

## Fix

Sort samples by the displayed gene order, as R does.

title: Oncoplot: two alteration classes in one cell keep only the last row
description:
When one gene and sample have two classes, the last row wins without a message (`pkg-r/R/oncoplot.R:120`, `pkg-py/src/plotomics/oncoplot.py:179-183`). TP53 in S1 as both Truncating and Missense draws only Missense, and which class shows depends on the row order.

## Fix

Mark the cell as multi-hit, as maftools does, or draw both classes.

title: Oncoplot wrappers rank genes by mutation rows, not by altered samples
description:
R (`pkg-r/R/oncoplot.R:222`, `table(g)`) and Python (`pkg-py/src/plotomics/oncoplot.py:31-32`, `Counter`) count rows, so a gene with several mutations in one sample ranks above a gene altered in more samples. With TTN three times in S1, and TP53 once in S1 and once in S2, TTN ranks first at 50%, above TP53 at 100%. The percentages are right; only the order is wrong.

## Fix

Count distinct samples per gene.

title: Oncoplot annotation values are matched by position, not by sample name
description:
When `samples` is not given, the columns are memo-sorted, but the annotation `values` are used in the order they were passed, and the names of a named vector are dropped (`pkg-r/R/oncoplot.R:152-163`, `pkg-py/src/plotomics/oncoplot.py:241-256`).

With the R test fixture and `values = c(S1 = "LumA", S2 = "Basal", S3 = "LumA", S4 = "Her2")`, the columns come out as S2, S1, S3, S4, and the strip shows LumA, Basal, LumA, Her2. The right order is Basal, LumA, LumA, Her2. There is no error. The tests always pass `samples`, which hides this.

## Fix

Match annotation values to samples by name (require names, or take a data frame with a sample column), and reorder them with the columns.

title: R km() and violin() drop group_colors when groups is not given
description:
`meta$groupColors` is set only inside `if (!is.null(groups))` (`pkg-r/R/violin.R:113-127`, `pkg-r/R/km.R:99-115`).

- violin: a text `group` column, the usual case and what `violin_density()` returns, with `groups = NULL` sends no colours, so the default palette is used.
- km: a data frame with a single curve drops `group_colors` the same way.

Python raises an error in the same case, so the two languages also disagree.

## Fix

Send `group_colors` whenever it is given, matched to the groups in the data.

title: KM: one risk_times value fails for a fit with several groups
description:
With one time point, `vapply` returns a vector, so `t()` builds a matrix with 1 row and one column per group (`pkg-r/R/km.R:223-231`). `km(survfit(Surv(time, status) ~ sex, lung), risk_times = 365)` stops with "`risk_counts` must have one column per `risk_times` entry". Two or more times work.

## Fix

Keep the result a matrix with one column per time, whatever the number of times.

title: KM curves stop at the last given point when the input lists event times only
description:
The component draws only the points it is given and never extends a group's last step to its last censor time (`pkg-js/src/components/km.ts:385-397`, censor ticks at `:403-415`). Censor ticks after the last point are drawn with no curve under them.

The R survfit path is fine, because `fit$time` includes censor-only times. A table built from event times only, such as `summary(fit)` with its defaults or a hand-built table, stops early. In the dev demo, two curves end near 96 months while the risk table shows 5 and 54 subjects still at risk at 100 months.

## Fix

Extend each curve with a flat step to the later of its last point and its last censor tick, or to a `max_time` given by the caller.

title: KM: with y_from_zero = FALSE the confidence band runs past the axis
description:
`yMin()` (`pkg-js/src/components/km.ts:254-260`) looks only at `surv`, not at `lower`, and the canvas is not clipped to the panel (`:357-380`). With a lowest survival of 0.42 (axis from 0.35) and a lower bound of 0.2, the band runs through the tick labels and the risk table and off the bottom of the widget.

## Fix

Include `lower` in the y range, or clip the canvas to the plot panel.

title: KM: rows sorted by time across groups draw mixed curves
KM: a custom groups order in R scrambles the at-risk table
description:
`bv_tidy_survfit` builds the `risk_counts` rows in survfit strata order (`pkg-r/R/km.R:223-231`). `km()` sends them by position and checks only the row count (`km.R:126-135`), and the JS reads row g against `meta.groups[g]` (`pkg-js/src/components/km.ts:460-468`).

With strata a (n = 6) and b (n = 10), `km(fit, groups = c("b", "a"))` shows row b as 6 5 3 1 0 0 and row a as 10 9 7 5 3 1, which are the counts of the other group.

## Fix

Reorder the risk rows to match `groups` by stratum name, and test with a reversed order.

title: KM: risk table names are cut off, and the table space is reserved with no counts
description:
- The left gutter is a fixed 58 px (`pkg-js/src/components/km.ts:118`), and the risk-table row labels get no extra room. Each label ends at x = 50 and the first count is centred at x = 58 (`km.ts:462-472`), so a three-digit count touches its label ("intermediate140") and a label wider than 50 px is cut off at the left edge. The "number at risk" heading touches the "0" tick label.
- The risk-table space (34 px plus 16 px per group) is reserved even when there are no risk counts (`km.ts:121-123` against `:456`). That is the default in Python and for R data-frame input, so a blank band sits under the axis.
- The default x label is "months", which is wrong for data in days or years.

## Proposal

Size the label column from the longest group name, reserve the table only when counts exist, and use "time" as the default x label.

title: Treemap: colours change meaning on drill-in, and the font family is shared across instances
description:
- The palette is built again on every layout (`pkg-js/src/components/treemap.ts:238`), and `focus.copy()` (`:242`) cuts the parent chain that `topAncestorId` (`:128-133`) needs. At the root, A's genes are red and B's are green. After drilling into A, the A2 genes turn green. The comment at `:176` says colours stay the same across zoom.
- `_sharedFontFamily` is a module-level variable shared by all treemap instances (`treemap.ts:497`, `:545`).

title: Python Treemap rejects integer ids when the root parent is None
description:
pandas makes a parent column that holds None into float64, so a parent becomes "1.0" while the id is "1" (`pkg-py/src/plotomics/treemap.py:87-88`, `:161-169`).

```python
Treemap(pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2, 3, 4], "parent": [None, 1, 1, 2], "value": [0, 0, 5, 3]}))
# parent(s) not found among ids: 1.0, 2.0
```

The same data works in R.

## Fix

Convert whole-number floats back to integer text before matching ids.

title: Treemap groups have no labels, no colour key and no visible border
description:
- Labels are drawn only for leaves (`pkg-js/src/components/treemap.ts:334-352`), so top-level groups have no label.
- The tooltip shows only the leaf name and value (`:378-381`), not its group.
- Padding is the same 1 px at every level (`:243-247`), so group edges look like gene edges.
- There is no colour key in either `color_by` mode.
- With more groups than palette colours, touching groups share a colour (#113).

The dev demo with 12 groups shows a grid of blocks with no labels.

## Fix

Label top-level groups, add the group to the tooltip, use larger outer padding for groups (d3 `paddingOuter` or `paddingTop`), and add a colour key.

title: Treemap adds internal node values on top of their children
description:
`root.sum` (`pkg-js/src/components/treemap.ts:117-119`) adds each internal node's own value to the sum of its children. The R and Python docs say internal nodes "are summed automatically", which reads as if their own values are ignored. With P1 = 8 (g1 = 3, g2 = 5) and P2 = 2 (g3 = 2), the leaves fill only 49.7% of the plot, and 33% if the root is also given its total. The rest is blank and cannot be hovered.

## Fix

Sum leaf values only, or check that internal values are 0 and say so in the docs.

title: Treemap without a value column is blank
description:
The docs list `value` as optional, but without it the R and Python wrappers send all zeros (`pkg-r/R/treemap.R:113`, `pkg-py/src/plotomics/treemap.py:133`), and the component skips tiles with zero area (`pkg-js/src/components/treemap.ts:282`).

```r
treemap(data.frame(id = c("root", "P1", "g1", "g2"), parent = c(NA, "root", "P1", "P1")))
```

This shows only the breadcrumb, with no tiles, labels or hover.

## Fix

When no value is given, give each leaf a weight of 1, or make `value` required.

title: Volcano tooltip writes the gene label as raw HTML
description: `pkg-js/src/components/volcano.ts:180-182` writes the label into the tooltip's `innerHTML` without escaping it. A label such as `<unknown>` disappears from the tooltip, and markup in a label is rendered. embedding (`embedding.ts:399`) and spatial (`spatial.ts:248`) escape the label.

title: Volcano: setOptions({ theme }) does not update the canvas background
description: `applyColors` (`pkg-js/src/components/volcano.ts:271-278`) does not pass `backgroundColor` to regl-scatterplot, unlike embedding (`embedding.ts:721-722`). Switching to a dark theme gives light labels and grid over a white canvas.

title: Volcano gene labels overlap and run past the right edge
description:
Every label goes at (x + 4, y - 4) with `text-anchor="start"`, with no overlap check and no flip near the right edge (`pkg-js/src/components/volcano.ts:337-361`). With the default `label_top_n = 10` (up to 20 labels), labels near the top corners pile up into unreadable blocks, and labels on the right are cut off at the plot edge. The dev demo and the R help example of `volcano()` both show it.

## Fix

Drop or move labels that collide (lollipop has a `stackLabels` helper), and put labels to the left of points near the right edge.

title: Volcano mishandles p = 0 and missing p-values
description:
p = 0 is common: Seurat `FindMarkers` reports `p_val = 0`, and DESeq2 p-values can underflow. Then `-log10(p)` is Inf.

- Python: one Inf in y makes `paddedExtent` (`pkg-js/src/components/volcano.ts:82`) return [0, 1], so the y frame is [0, 1] and every point with y > 1 is off screen. With y = [4, 1, 8, Inf], the ticks run from 0 to 1 and the finite points sit far above the plot.
- R: Inf and NA arrive as null (#96) and are drawn at y = 0 in grey as not significant, so the strongest hit sits on the baseline. This example draws its last two genes at y = 0 in grey:

  ```r
  set.seed(1)
  df <- data.frame(x = c(rnorm(200), 3, -3), y = c(runif(200, 0, 4), Inf, NA), label = paste0("g", 1:202))
  volcano(df)
  ```

- Python NaN: `classify` (`volcano.ts:104`) counts a gene with NaN p and a large log2FC as a hit, because `NaN < yThresh` is false. The top-N sort (`:349`) and the bounds check (`:358`) let it take a label slot at y = "NaN". With x = [4, 2, -2], y = [NaN, 5, 5] and `labelTopN = 1`, the only "up" label goes to the NaN gene. DESeq2 sets p to NA for outlier genes and keeps their log2FC, so this input is normal.

## Fix

- Compute the y range from finite values only.
- Skip NaN and NA points: do not classify, label or draw them, and give their count in the existing warning.
- Keep y = +Inf: draw it at the top of the finite frame with a distinct marker, and classify it by x. In R, Inf cannot be told from NA once it is JSON null, so the wrapper has to cap +Inf before sending (for example at the largest finite value plus a margin) and send the capped rows as an index list.

title: Network: NaN coordinates, and a tooltip that stays after an update
description:
- Python passes NaN coordinates through with a warning (`pkg-py/src/plotomics/network.py:153-155`), `network-core.ts:130` copies them, and Sigma throws. In R, NA arrives as null, becomes 0, and the node is placed at (0, 0) without a message.
- `applyData` resets `hovered` but never hides the tooltip (`pkg-js/src/components/network.ts:231-238`), and the new Sigma instance never fires `leaveNode`, so a tooltip shown during a Shiny update stays on screen.

title: Network edge width is the raw weight in pixels
description:
`size: e.weight` (`pkg-js/src/components/network-core.ts:155`) uses the weight as it is, while the docs say the weight is "mapped to edge width". STRING scores from 400 to 999 give edges hundreds of pixels wide that cover the graph, and weights from 0 to 1 all fall under Sigma's minimum edge thickness, so the weight has no visible effect.

## Fix

Map the absolute weight to a width range, for example 0.5 to 4 px.

title: Network: negative edge weights crash the layout
description:
`weight` goes to ForceAtlas2 as the attraction weight (`pkg-js/src/components/network-core.ts:155`, `:176-181`). Negative weights make the layout diverge to NaN, and the Sigma constructor (`network.ts:165`) throws:

```
Sigma: Coordinates of node N1 are invalid. A node must have a numeric 'x' and 'y' attribute.
```

A correlation network with weights from -0.9 to 0.9 never renders:

```r
set.seed(1)
nodes <- data.frame(id = paste0("N", 1:40))
edges <- data.frame(source = paste0("N", sample(1:40, 80, TRUE)), target = paste0("N", sample(1:40, 80, TRUE)), weight = runif(80, -0.9, 0.9))
edges <- edges[edges$source != edges$target, ]
network(nodes, edges)
```

Neither R nor Python rejects negative weights.

## Fix

Pass `abs(weight)` (or another transform that is never negative) to the layout and keep the sign for display, or reject negative weights with a clear message.

title: Network PNG and SVG export return an empty image
description:
With nodes and edges on screen, `exportPNG(1)` on a 600 x 400 network returns an image in a single colour, with no nodes and no edges.

Sigma draws nodes and edges into WebGL canvases created with `preserveDrawingBuffer: false`. `compositeCanvas` (`pkg-js/src/components/network.ts:298-315`) copies those canvases with `drawImage` without rendering first, so the browser hands back cleared buffers. `exportSVG` uses the same composite.

```js
const net = createNetwork(el, { data: { columns: { id, x, y }, meta: { edges } } });
const png = await net.exportPNG(1); // every pixel is the background colour
```

## Fix

Render and copy the layers in the same frame (call sigma's `refresh()` and read the canvases before returning to the event loop), or create the layers with `preserveDrawingBuffer: true`. Add a browser test that counts drawn pixels in the export, like `test/browser/scatter-fit.test.ts`.

title: A Shiny re-render keeps old option values when an argument goes back to NULL
description:
On a re-render, the htmlwidgets binding calls `setOptions` with the new options (`pkg-js/src/lib/umd.ts:50-55`), and each component merges them over the previous ones (`{ ...prev, ...next }`). The R wrappers leave NULL arguments out of the payload, so an option that was set and is then cleared keeps its old value. The comment at `pkg-r/R/heatmap.R:73-74` says NULL is sent as JSON null, but `options$vmin <- NULL` removes the key.

## Examples

- `bioheatmap(m, vmin = if (input$clamp) -2 else NULL)`: after the clamp is turned off, the colour range stays at -2 to 2.
- `renderDotplot` with `value_domain = c(0, 10)` and then `value_domain = NULL`: the colour bar still reads 0 to 10.
- `hic(m, vmax = 5, label = "chr1")` and then `hic(m)`: vmax stays 5 and the titles stay "chr1".
- embedding: switching the colour column from a factor (levels 0, 1, 2) to a character column (T, B) gives a legend of 0, 1, 2, T, B, because `categories` is only sent for a factor.
- `theme`, volcano `colors` and every other optional argument behave the same way.

The Python path does the same when a key is dropped from `w.options`.

In the same re-render, `setData` runs before `setOptions`. So the clustermap clusters twice (#136) and hic applies a changed `symmetric` one render late (#126).

## Fix

After the first `renderValue`, build the options from the component defaults plus the new payload, not from the previous options. One call that sets data and options together also removes the double work.

title: R sends one-element vectors as single JSON values, so one-row input breaks the plot
description:
htmlwidgets serialises the payload with `auto_unbox = TRUE`, so a vector of length 1 reaches the browser as a bare value, not an array. Every R wrapper wraps `meta` in `I()`, but the data columns and several vectors inside `meta` are not wrapped. The JS then reads `.length` of a number, or indexes a string one character at a time.

```r
htmlwidgets:::toJSON(list(columns = list(x = 175), meta = list(classes = "missense")))
#> {"columns":{"x":175},"meta":{"classes":"missense"}}
```

## Effects

- oncoplot with one alteration class crashes with `TypeError: classes(...).map is not a function`, for example `oncoplot(data.frame(gene = c("TP53", "KRAS"), sample = c("S1", "S2"), class = "missense"))`, which is the shape of the package's own Shiny example. With one gene, the row label is the first letter of the gene and the frequency reads 0.0%. A 1x1 oncoplot shows an altered cell as empty.
- volcano, embedding, spatial, dotplot and lollipop draw no points when the data frame has one row, which a Shiny filter can easily produce. `volcano(data.frame(x = 2, y = 5, label = "TP53"))` shows empty axes from -1 to 1 and 0 to 1. A lollipop with one variant draws no head, shows a y-axis maximum of 1 and labels the variant with one letter.
- A one-column heatmap or clustermap loses its column label (`"colLabels":"s1"` fails the `Array.isArray` check), and a 1x1 matrix draws nothing.
- hic draws an empty map for a 1x1 matrix or a single contact.
- upset with one intersection is blank, including `upset_intersections(m, max_n = 1)`.
- network with one edge reads the ids one character at a time and drops the edge. One node `"TP53"` becomes four nodes. A one-colour `palette = "#ff0000"` gives node colours "#", "f", "f".
- profile with one bar fails the same way.
- `theme = list(categorical = "#hex")` sends a string where the JS expects an array.

## Where

- `pkg-r/R/utils.R:22-27` (`plotomics_widget`)
- `pkg-r/R/oncoplot.R:133-146`, `lollipop.R:115-117`, `profile.R:72-76`, `volcano.R:63`, `embedding.R:95`, `spatial.R:94`, `heatmap.R:55-66`, `clustermap.R:87-97`, `hic.R:70`, `hic.R:101-103`, `upset.R:100`, `network.R:104-150`

## Fix

Wrap every column vector and every vector inside `meta` and `options` that the JS reads as an array in `I()`, once, inside `plotomics_widget`, so no component can miss it. Add an R test per component with one row.

title: Hi-C: smaller defects in zoom, tooltip, theme and cleanup
description:
- One Inf cell blanks the whole map: `autoVmax` returns Infinity (`pkg-js/src/components/hic.ts:132-153`), so every finite value normalises to 0. R and Python only warn.
- Zooming in on a matrix with n < 4 moves the view off the matrix: the span is clamped to 4 bins with no `lo < 0` guard (`hic.ts:719-731`). One zoom step on a 3x3 matrix gives the view [-1, 3].
- When zoomed, the tooltip reports off-screen bins while the pointer is over the margins or the colour bar (`hic.ts:693-701`). Hovering the colour bar shows bin 223 by 149 with 224 contacts.
- A `theme.background` that is not hex, such as "white" or "rgb(...)", is read as black (`hic.ts:889-902`).
- The anonymous `mouseleave` listener is never removed on destroy (`hic.ts:740`).

title: Hi-C ignores colormap = "rdbu" and forces a negative vmin to 0
description:
R and Python accept `colormap = "rdbu"` (`pkg-r/R/hic.R:20`, `:48`; `pkg-py/src/plotomics/hic.py:81`), but `colormapLUT` ignores its name (`pkg-js/src/components/hic.ts:278-288`), so the map and the colour bar are always viridis. The shader and the colour bar also use `max(0, vmin)` (`hic.ts:407`, `:594-596`, `:631`).

So `hic(oe_log2, colormap = "rdbu", transform = "linear", vmin = -2, vmax = 2)` draws viridis, with every negative value as background.

## Fix

Build the lookup from the named ramp, and allow a negative vmin with the linear transform (the log transform keeps the floor at 0).

title: Python HiC reads a 3x3 nested list as a sparse triplet
description:
`HiC([[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6], [7, 8, 9]])` sends `n = 7` with columns i, j and v, and draws a 7x7 map with 3 contacts (`pkg-py/src/plotomics/hic.py:188-189`). A 4x4 nested list is read correctly as a dense matrix.

## Fix

Treat a nested list as dense unless `i`, `j` and `v` are passed, or ask for an explicit format when the input has 3 columns.

title: Hi-C: one NaN bin blanks its whole block in the zoomed-out view
description:
The level-of-detail pyramid pools bins with a plain mean (`pkg-js/src/components/hic.ts:209`), so one NaN makes the whole pooled block NaN. Balanced cooler matrices mark filtered bins as NaN.

With n = 2000 and 8% of bins masked, 16.6% of the cells are NaN at level 0, but 51% at level 2, which is the level used for the full view of a 418 px plot at DPR 1 (31% at DPR 2). About half of the overview is drawn as background.

## Fix

Pool with a mean that skips NaN.

title: Hi-C: changing symmetric with setOptions has no effect until the next setData
description:
The sparse triplet is turned into a dense matrix only in `applyData` (`pkg-js/src/components/hic.ts:456`, `:817-834`). With a sparse contact `(0, 1) = 7`, `setOptions({ symmetric: false })` still shows 7 when hovering cell (1, 0). It shows 0 only after another `setData`.

In an R Shiny re-render, `setData` runs before `setOptions`, so a changed `symmetric` takes effect one render late.

## Fix

Build the dense matrix again when `symmetric` changes.

title: Hi-C axis and tooltip labels show wrong coordinates
description:
`formatCoord` (`pkg-js/src/components/hic.ts:270-275`) strips trailing zeros with `.replace(/\.?0+$/, "")`, which also strips zeros when there is no decimal point:

```js
formatCoord(100000);    // "1kb", the right label is "100kb"
formatCoord(120000);    // "12kb"
formatCoord(150000000); // "15Mb"
formatCoord(200000000); // "2Mb"
```

On chr1 at 250 kb bins, the full-view ticks read `0, 25Mb, 50Mb, 75Mb, 1Mb, 125Mb, 15Mb, 175Mb, 2Mb, 225Mb`. The tooltip uses the same function (`hic.ts:703-704`).

`toPrecision(3)` also makes labels collapse when zoomed in. A whole chromosome at 10 kb, zoomed to bins 2500 to 2540, gives `25Mb, 25.1Mb, 25.1Mb, 25.1Mb, 25.2Mb`, and bins 2501, 2502 and 2503 all show "25Mb" in the tooltip. With no `bin_size`, a window of fewer than 6 bins gets half-bin ticks rounded to `10, 11, 11, 12, 12`, which includes the default view of any matrix with n < 6.

## Fix

Strip zeros only after a decimal point, and pick the number of decimals from the tick step (or from the bin size for the tooltip). Add unit tests for `formatCoord`.

title: Hi-C map is always blank because the float texture needs a WebGL extension that is never enabled
description:
`createREGL` is called without `extensions` or `optionalExtensions` (`pkg-js/src/components/hic.ts:336-339`), and `levelTexture` then asks for `type: "float"` (`hic.ts:424-433`). The checked regl build, which the R and Python bundles both ship, throws:

```
(regl) you must enable the OES_texture_float extension in order to use floating point textures.
```

The map stays blank and the colour bar shows 0 to 1, in every browser and in JS, R and Python. The `hic` demo in `pnpm dev` and the R help example of `hic()` both show it.

`createHic` throws from its init block, so no instance is returned. The canvas, the SVG and the tooltip stay in the element, with a `window` mouseup listener and a live WebGL context. In Shiny, `inst` stays null (`pkg-js/src/lib/umd.ts:50-52`), so every `renderValue` builds the component again on the same element and adds another canvas, SVG, tooltip and WebGL context.

`min: "linear"` on a float texture also needs `OES_texture_float_linear`, which iOS does not have.

## Fix

- Upload a uint8 luminance texture normalised on the CPU. The colour lookup has 256 entries, so nothing visible is lost, and no extension is needed. Map any value above vmin to at least 1 so it does not fall to the background, rebuild the textures when vmin, vmax, vmaxPercentile or transform change, and pool raw values before normalising.
- Or request `optionalExtensions: ["OES_texture_float", "OES_texture_float_linear"]`, use `min: "nearest"` when float-linear is missing, and keep the uint8 path as the fallback.
- Wrap the WebGL work in try/catch with a broken flag, as `heatmap.ts` does with `reglBroken`, so `createHic` and `setData` never throw.
- Add a browser test that mounts hic and counts drawn pixels, like `test/browser/scatter-fit.test.ts`.

title: Profile: a NaN value with as_fraction draws raw values with percent labels
description:
In Python (R rejects NaN), a NaN value makes the total NaN (`pkg-js/src/components/profile.ts:195-196`), so the bars are drawn from raw values while the axis shows percentages, for example "5000%".

## Fix

Leave values that are not finite out of the total, or reject them in Python as R does.

title: Heatmap and clustermap: smaller colour and redraw defects
description:
- `setData` with empty values keeps the old image: `render()` returns before clearing the WebGL canvas (`pkg-js/src/components/heatmap.ts:398-403`).
- The clustermap paints cells in viridis for every colormap except "rdbu" (`clustermap.ts:320-323`), while the legend uses `ramp(opts.colormap)` (`:468`). So `ltc` or `ltcdiv` give cells and a legend that do not match. The heatmap treats only "rdbu" as diverging (`heatmap.ts:366`).
- With rdbu and only one of vmin or vmax set, the heatmap colour scale is no longer centred on 0 (`heatmap.ts:154`), so some negative values show red. The middle label of the legend still reads 0.
- With more rows than plot pixels, both components sample the nearest row, so 5000 rows in a 400 px plot draw about 1 row in 12 and a single outlier row can disappear.

title: Default heatmap and clustermap to a diverging colormap when z_score is on
description:
With `z_score = TRUE` the values are centred on 0, but both components keep the sequential viridis map by default, so values above and below the mean get similar colours.

## Proposal

Use `rdbu` by default when `z_score` is on and no colormap is given.

title: Small differences between the R, Python and JS front ends
description:
- dotplot colour bar title: JS falls back to "value" (`dotplot.ts:223`, `:348`), while R and Python send "mean expression" (`dotplot.R:44`, `dotplot.py:75`). Use "mean expression" in all three.
- heatmap has no option for the colour bar title (fixed "value" or "z-score", `heatmap.ts:514-517`), while clustermap has `legend_title`.
- The colormaps on offer differ: dotplot and spatial allow `ltc` and `ltcdiv`, the other components only `viridis` and `rdbu`.
- Helpers exist in one language only: R has `upset_intersections()`, `violin_density()` and survfit input to `km()`, and Python has only `memo_sort`. Python `Km` takes `censor` as an argument, while R gets it only from a survfit object.
- The R names `bioheatmap()` and `bioprofile()` do not match Python's `Heatmap` and `Profile`.
- lollipop `label_top_n` (default 12) exists only in the wrappers, which compute `meta.labelIndex`, so a JS user gets no labels. volcano uses `labelTopN` with a default of 10 in JS.
- R and Python break ties differently: oncoplot class order ties sort by name in R and by first appearance in Python, and samples and levels use locale collation in R and code-point order in Python. The same data can get different colours in each language.
- igv: `genome=None` drops the key (`igv.py:68-69`), so the JS falls back to "hg38".
- gosling: `theme` is Gosling's theme, while in every other widget it is a plotomics theme.

title: Spatial: default spot size and legend placement
description:
The default `spot_diameter` is 4 image px (`pkg-js/src/components/spatial.ts:177`, `pkg-r/R/spatial.R:58`, `pkg-py/src/plotomics/spatial.py:91`). On a full-resolution image, the contain fit shrinks spots to the 1 px floor (`spatial.ts:116-118`).

The legend sits at width - 128 with no background (`spatial.ts:388-396`), so it overlaps the image at narrow widths, and labels longer than about 18 characters are cut off.

## Proposal

When no diameter is given, derive it from the median distance between neighbouring spots, and draw the legend in a reserved gutter.

title: Network shows no node labels at the starting zoom
description:
`labelThreshold` defaults to 8 and `defaultNodeSize` to 4 (`pkg-js/src/components/network.ts:96-97`). Sigma skips a label when the rendered node size is below the threshold, and at zoom 1 the rendered size is 4, so no label shows until about 4x zoom. Labels use sigma's default 14 px size, not the theme font size, and there is no legend for the node groups.

## Proposal

Set `labelThreshold` to 4 (sigma's label grid already thins labels), take the label size from the theme, and add a group legend.

title: Element height: plain JS draws into a 0 px box, and the htmlwidgets binding fixes the height in px
description:
- `pkg-js/src/core/dom.ts:61-66`: when the container has 0 height, `measure()` falls back to 640 x 480, but no component sets the element's height or watches for resizes. A plain-JS or Quarto OJS div with no CSS height gets a 480 px drawing inside a 0 px box, which overlaps the content below it. The wrappers are not affected: anywidget sets the host height (`anywidget.ts:20`) and htmlwidgets sets the element height.
- `pkg-js/src/lib/umd.ts:42` sets `el.style.height` to the first height in px. `volcanoOutput("v", height = "100vh")`, `calc(...)` or a percentage loses its CSS height, so the plot no longer follows changes to the window height. bslib fill containers still grow the element.

## Fix

Set the fallback height on the element when it measures 0, and attach a ResizeObserver through a shared helper. In the binding, leave a CSS height alone when one is set.

title: Binary transport: big-endian arrays, schema-only changes and sub-view bounds
description:
- `pkg-py/src/plotomics/_base.py:97-100` and `:153`: a big-endian float64 array, as from h5py or FITS, takes the fast path because `dtype.name` is "float64", and `tobytes()` keeps big-endian order. `np.array([1, 2.5, -3], dtype=">f8")` is read in JS as `[3.0e-319, 5.4e-321, 1.1e-320]`.
- `pkg-js/src/lib/anywidget.ts:42-47` listens for buffer changes but not for `change:schema`. Setting `w.buffer` and then `w.schema` without `hold_sync` decodes the new buffer with the old schema, and the later schema change triggers nothing. No public API does this, so it only happens when traits are set by hand.
- `pkg-js/src/core/transport.ts:82`: the bounds check in `decodeColumns` uses the parent ArrayBuffer, not the end of the DataView. A schema that asks for more values than the view holds reads the neighbouring bytes and does not throw. `pack_columns` always writes a consistent schema.

## Fix

Convert to little-endian before packing, listen for `change:schema`, and check bounds against `view.byteOffset + view.byteLength`.

title: Gridlines are drawn on top of the data in volcano, upset, dotplot, profile and embedding
description:
The gridlines are SVG lines in the overlay, which sits above the canvas, so a pale line crosses every bar, dot and point under it.

- volcano: the SVG is added after the canvas (`volcano.ts:144-145`), with grid lines at `:292` and `:301`.
- upset: grid lines at `upset.ts:321`, SVG added after the canvas at `:173-174`.
- dotplot: `dotplot.ts:304-309`.
- profile: the horizontal grid lines cross the bars.
- embedding with `showAxes`: `embedding.ts:544` and `:550`.

## Fix

Draw the grid on the canvas before the marks, or split the SVG into a layer under the canvas and a layer above it. The canvas background is opaque (`theme.background`), so a layer under it also needs a transparent canvas.
